western.temperament: Caring, artistic, flexible, perceptive, intuitive and spiritually minded. Shadow: indecisive, easily fooled, emotional ups and downs, can be sly. Devoted, affectionate partner who mixes fantasy with reality; drawn to purposeful work over money.
western.modality: Mutable; twelfth sign; opposite sign Virgo. Symbol: two fish tied by a cord, from the myth of Aphrodite and Eros turning into fish to escape Typhon

chinese.temperament: Clever, quick-witted, versatile, fast learner, creative and engaging. Shadow: pranks that can hurt, restless, sly, hard to trust; easily bored in love until the right partner, then fully committed. Career fits listed by China Highlights include science, engineering, trading, film directing.
chinese.clash: Tiger (Wikipedia also lists Pig as a six-harm pair)

symbolism.meaning: The octopus and squid (heʻe) are kinolau, body forms, of Kanaloa, lord of the ocean, associated with voyaging and healing; the Kumulipo chant records Kanaloa born as a heʻe. Wikipedia adds a Hawaiian creation account in which the octopus is the lone survivor of a previous age. Tell it as Hawaiian tradition, credited, and do not lay a 'you' reading over it.

The common name comes from the title elephant of Disney's 1941 film Dumbo: two ear-like fins sit above the eyes. Chinese popular usage follows the same joke: 小飛象章魚 xiǎo fēixiàng zhāngyú, 'little flying elephant octopus'. Trivia only; brief says never use as the hook.

Octopus imagery appears on Minoan coins possibly as early as 1650 BCE and on Mycenaean pottery around 1200 to 1100 BCE: the octopus as an emblem of seafaring peoples. Generic octopus lore, not dumbo-specific.
In the Asuka-era legend Taishokan, a woman diver fights an octopus to win back a stolen jewel from the sea floor; the tale inspired woodblock prints. Generic octopus lore.
The octopus as monster: Akkorokamui (Ainu), the kraken (Norse), possibly the Gorgons. Opposite in mood to the gentle dumbo; useful only as contrast.

'Dumbo octopus spirit animal' meanings (gentleness, adaptability, emotional depth) found only on totem blogs; no traditional source. No dumbo-specific folklore exists that we could find: the animal was barely known before deep-sea cameras.

fusion.temperament: Our reading: mutable Water (Pisces) meets yang Metal (Monkey). Metal generates Water in the five-phase cycle, so the Monkey's quick mind feeds the Pisces depth rather than fighting it. The dumbo is the clever one who lives far down: a gentle drifter with a problem-solver's brain, swimming by its 'ears' where the light never reaches.
fusion.gifts: Our reading: comfort in pressure and dark that sends others back up; inventive solutions found by hovering patiently over a problem; a soft, disarming presence (the cartoon name) that hides real competence; making things that stand on their own once released, like the cirrate's fully competent hatchlings.
fusion.shadow: Our reading: no ink. Few defenses beyond distance and depth, so retreat becomes the only plan. Pisces escapism plus Monkey restlessness: drifting from one deep interest to the next, explaining nothing to people at the surface. The Monkey's sly streak can show as charm used to avoid being pinned down.
fusion.love: Our reading: Pisces devotion with a Monkey's need for play. Slow to settle, then fully loyal (both sources note commitment once the right partner appears). Needs a partner curious enough to come down to their depth and light enough to laugh there.
fusion.money: Our reading: the continuous spawner. Earns in steady small batches rather than seasonal windfalls; Monkey cleverness spots odd opportunities, Pisces idealism forgets to invoice. Works best with automatic, low-attention saving.
fusion.conflict: Our reading: lifts off the bottom and glides away rather than fight; no ink, no cloud of drama. When cornered the Monkey answers with wit. Risk: the other person thinks it is resolved when the dumbo has simply left the depth.

candidate_lines: You carry no ink. When the dark gets crowded you trust the slow beat of your fins and a mind quick enough to change course before anyone sees you turn.
Several feelings sit inside you at different stages, the way a dumbo carries eggs at every stage at once, and none of them waits for the right season.
Monkey wit at the bottom of the sea: you solve the thing quietly in the dark, then come up with a joke so nobody asks how deep you went.
You leave what you make on the coral and drift on. People find it grown and standing on its own, and rarely trace it back to you.
In love you need someone willing to come down past the last of the light, where your fins open and you move the way you were built to.
Small talk at the surface wears you out in minutes. Hand you one strange, heavy question and you will hover over it for hours, content.

fact_audit.fact: Header hanzi 小飛象章魚 (rail__han and serial-han), shown with pinyin xiǎofēixiàng zhāngyú lower on the page
fact_audit.note: Popular Chinese name, 'little flying elephant octopus', used by Greenpeace Taiwan for the dumbo octopus. The formal genus name on Chinese Wikipedia (zh-tw) is 菸灰蛸屬 yānhuīshāo shǔ (simplified 烟灰蛸属). Keep 小飛象章魚 for readers; it is long for a rail glyph. Make sure pinyin sits beside the header too.

Too narrow. Wikipedia gives roughly 1,000 to 7,000 m, with species ranges from 480 to 1,993 m (G. greeni) up to about 4,847 m (G. boylei), and ROV sightings at 960, 1,250 and 2,108 m. Say 'mostly 1,000 m and deeper, down to nearly 7,000 m'. Same fix for Working Nature and Mirror lines that pin it to 3,000 m.

fact_audit.fact: Intro: 'drift through the water column of the hadal zone'
fact_audit.note: The hadal zone starts around 6,000 m (trenches). 3,000 to 4,000 m is bathyal to abyssal. Only one dumbo sighting (6,957 m) is hadal. Drop 'hadal zone'.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 1: ear-like fins are primary locomotion, 'the only octopuses to use fins as primary locomotion rather than jet propulsion'
fact_audit.note: Fins as main propulsion is right for Grimpoteuthis, but all cirrate octopods (suborder Cirrina, e.g. Opisthoteuthis, Cirroteuthis, Cirrothauma) have fins and swim with them. Wikipedia also notes they crawl on the bottom and can pump through their webs. Say 'like other finned (cirrate) octopuses'.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 2: deepest living octopus, 'confirmed at depths exceeding 7,000 meters', 'the extreme of any known cephalopod'
fact_audit.note: The confirmed record is 6,957 m (Java Trench, filmed April 2019; Jamieson and Vecchione 2020, Marine Biology; Guinness). A 7,279 m Cayman trawl record is uncertain. Deepest octopus and deepest unequivocal cephalopod: OK. 'Exceeding 7,000 m confirmed': wrong.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 3: no ink sac, 'because bioluminescent darkness makes ink-based concealment functionally useless'
fact_audit.note: No ink sac is confirmed (cirrates generally lack one; they also lack innervated chromatophores and cannot change colour). The reason given is our inference, not sourced; present the 'because' as a reading or drop it.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 4: females carry eggs at multiple stages, reproduction continuous across the year
fact_audit.note: Wikipedia: cirrates are continuous spawners with eggs at various stages and no seasonality, but this was confirmed mainly in Opisthoteuthis, not Grimpoteuthis. Add 'like related finned octopuses'. Extra sourced detail: eggs are laid one or two at a time on deep-sea octocorals, unguarded; hatchlings are fully competent.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 5: photoreceptors tuned to bioluminescent wavelengths; nervous system calibrated to pressure waves, chemical gradients and specific deep-sea light spectra
fact_audit.note: No source found. Wikipedia's Grimpoteuthis page says nothing on vision. A related dumbo, Cirrothauma murrayi, is called the 'blind octopod' because its eyes lack a lens and cannot form images (NOAA). Reads like generated detail; cut.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 6: encountered 'perhaps a few hundred times'; almost nothing known about lifespan, behaviour, population
fact_audit.note: No count found. 'Little known' is fair (mating never observed, feeding not seen directly), but Wikipedia gives an average lifespan of 3 to 5 years, so 'nothing known about lifespan' overstates. Drop the number.

fact_audit.fact: Hero: 'It lives at 13,000 feet' and test intro 'in total darkness at 13,000 feet'
fact_audit.note: About 3,960 m; inside the range, but presents one depth as the home. Soften to 'down to 13,000 feet and beyond'.

fact_audit.fact: Proverb 靜水流深 jìng shuǐ liú shēn, 'still waters run deep', tied to the Monkey year
fact_audit.note: The page labels the year tie as its own, which is fine. But no source shows a classical Chinese origin; the saying is traced to Latin (Curtius Rufus) and English use from 1400, and Chinese sources we opened give 靜水流深 as the literal translation of the English proverb. Do not present it as a Chinese proverb. Native near-equivalents: 深藏不露 shēn cáng bù lù.

fact_audit.fact: Habitat section: nuummite is 'the oldest stone on earth, 3 billion years'
fact_audit.note: Not an animal fact but a printed claim. Nuummite's parent rock formed about 2.8 billion years ago (Greenland); Wikipedia does not call it the oldest stone, and older rocks exist. Cut 'oldest stone on earth'.

fact_audit.fact: Page sources: Villanueva et al. 2002 (planktonic stages of benthic octopuses) and IUCN Grimpoteuthis boylei
fact_audit.note: Not opened. A paper on planktonic stages of benthic (shallow) octopuses is unlikely to support any dumbo fact on the page; the relevant Villanueva work is the 1997 cirrate locomotion study cited by Wikipedia. Replace with s6, s7.
Page has no star assignment; it says a chart is cast from lunar birth date and hour. Nothing to fix.
